tools.name: set_meshes
tools.description: Replace the whole &MESH deck with an explicit list of meshes (multi-mesh). Passing a single mesh reverts the project to single-mesh mode. config.mesh (the union bounding box) and the OPEN-boundary vents are kept consistent by the app. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes; for shape-driven placement prefer auto_multimesh.

meshes.description: Meshes that together tile the domain, in order.

id.description: Optional mesh ID (must be unique, e.g. M1)

tools.name: slice_mesh
tools.description: Split one mesh into two at a plane (multi-mesh cutter). The coordinate snaps to that mesh's own grid lines, cell size is preserved on both halves, and OPEN vents crossing the plane are split too. Slicing the single mesh turns the project into a multi-mesh deck. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

axis.description: Axis normal to the cut plane

coord.description: Cut position (m). Snapped to the nearest grid line of that mesh.

tools.name: merge_meshes
tools.description: Merge several meshes back into one (inverse of slice_mesh). Succeeds only when the selected meshes do not overlap and their union is exactly a box. When their cell sizes differ, `choice` picks which size the result uses; the union must divide into a whole number of those cells. Use list_meshes for index numbers.

indices.description: Mesh indices to merge (2 or more)

choice.description: Cell size to keep when the meshes differ: 'coarse' (larger cells, fewer) or 'fine'.

tools.name: auto_multimesh
tools.description: Build a multi-mesh deck from the OBSTRUCTION geometry. It measures the fluid gap everywhere (obstacles minus HOLEs, so doorways stay open), gives narrow places 3+ cells across and open places the default wide cell, then merges equal-size regions into boxes cut on obstacle faces so walls stay on mesh boundaries. Wall slabs up to 2 cells thick are absorbed into a neighbour. Cell sizes are quantised to min_cell x 2^k; an overlapping, gapped or misaligned deck is refused, not committed. The domain may grow to a multiple of the coarsest cell; OPEN vents follow. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify the result with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05. Must be > 0; it is the bottom of the 2^k ladder.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

tools.name: auto_cutcell_mesh
tools.description: Build a cut-cell multi-mesh deck from &GEOM triangulated shapes (plus OBSTs). Cells shrink where the fluid gap is narrow (gap / gap_cells), the GEOM surface band always gets the finest cell so the engine keeps its cut-cell wall physics there, sharp curvature gets one level finer, and levels change at most 2:1 between neighbouring blocks. Cell sizes are min_cell x 2^k. If the deck has no GEOM this is identical to auto_multimesh. Over budget it relaxes curvature, buffer, gap_cells, then raises min_cell and reports what it changed; a gapped, overlapping or misaligned deck is refused. Engine constraints (engine multimesh ratio_union_grid): (1) every mesh must use CUBIC cells whose size is the finest cell x 2^k (k in 1,2,4,8,16); (2) every mesh boundary and the union extent must land on a fine-grid index that is a multiple of the LARGEST ratio actually used; (3) meshes must tile the domain with no overlap and no gap; (4) a 1:4 or larger ratio makes the engine print an experimental-feature warning and switches it to per-mesh storage (MM2) plus the composite block-CG v2 pressure solve, both automatically. Verify with list_meshes.

min_cell.description: Finest cell size (m), e.g. 0.05 — used on the GEOM surface band and in narrow gaps.

max_cell.description: Coarsest cell size (m), e.g. 0.2. Rounded DOWN to min_cell x 2^k.

tools.name: spr_set_head_spray
tools.description: Set per-head spray settings on one or many sprinkler heads — pipe-network heads, obstacle sprinklers and DEVC sprinklers alike (the GUI spray dialog "this head only" path). Pick heads with all / group (interlock or deluge group) / network_of_node / head_ids / node_ids / obstacle_ids / device_ids. profile_id links them to a shared profile (pipe heads take its K, activation temperature and RTI unless keep_head_values). prop / part override single FDS keys for these heads only; inherit lists keys to hand back to the profile (prop/part keys or orientation, rotation, pipe_index, activation); reset drops every override. orientation / rotation / pipe_index / activation are DEVC values. head_type applies to pipe heads (upright still sprays down). All heads are checked first; if any would be an FDS error nothing changes. Pipe heads whose K changed need spr_run_calc then spr_apply_to_fds.

all.description: every sprinkler head in the project (pipe network, obstacle and DEVC sprinklers)

group.description: sprinkler interlock/deluge group id or name — all its members

network_of_node.description: pipe node id — every head in the pipe network connected to it

node_ids.description: pipe-network sprinkler node ids (all heads on them)

profile_id.description: Link the heads to this spray profile

keep_head_values.description: With profile_id: pipe heads keep their own K / activation temperature / RTI

reset.description: Drop every per-head spray override first (pipe heads: K / activation / RTI back to the profile)

prop.description: Per-head &PROP overrides — same keys and units as spr_upsert_spray_profile.prop

part.description: Per-head &PART droplet overrides — same keys and units as spr_upsert_spray_profile.part

inherit.description: Keys to remove from the heads so they follow the profile again

orientation.description: DEVC ORIENTATION spray axis (default [0,0,-1]; sidewall e.g. [1,0,0])

pipe_index.description: DEVC PIPE_INDEX (pipe network number for PRESSURE_RAMP / OPEN NOZZLES)

activation.description: How the head opens: link (heat, default), time (DEVC TIME + SETPOINT), ctrl (CTRL_ID), initial (open at t=0).

ctrl_id.description: CTRL id (mode ctrl, or extra condition for link)

delay_s.description: s opening delay after link activation (dry/pre-action)

initial_state.description: INITIAL_STATE with time/ctrl (open first, close at SETPOINT)

tools.name: spr_apply_to_fds
tools.description: Apply the hydraulic pipe-network sprinklers to the FDS model: for every sprinkler node (with a head and calc results from spr_run_calc), creates/replaces DEVC (SPRINKLER LINK TEMPERATURE) + PROP + PART entries using the calculated nozzle flow and pressure. Run spr_run_calc first.

tools.name: spr_analyze_drawing
tools.description: Read a sprinkler / water-spray piping drawing (.dxf, .dwg, .pdf, .zip of drawings, .png/.jpg) and recognise a candidate pipe network. Isometric (ISO) drawings: scale from DIMENSION entities, pipe linetype, bends, flange/valve gaps bridged, nozzle stems, line-number / reducer / valve labels, 3D reconstruction (X,Y horizontal, Z up, inlet = origin), nominal sizes from labels and flange rings. Plan drawings: pipe layers + head symbols at one height. Returns a summary with candidateId, open ends (drain candidates), reference (dashed, other-system) labels, exclusion hints, runs and ambiguities to ask the user about. Attached chat files arrive as "[첨부 도면] name path=… candidateId=…". PDFs with outlined text set needsVision (read the page image instead). show=segments|nodes|runs|tags|components lists details (ids, offset, limit, component). Then call spr_import_network.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the drawing file

candidateId.description: Id from an earlier analysis or the chat attachment (re-use without re-reading)

options.description: Re-analysis options: projection (isometric|plan), pipeLinetypes / referenceLinetypes / detailLinetypes (DXF linetype names), layers / excludeLayers, scaleMmPerUnit (drawing unit → mm when the drawing has no DIMENSION), lineNoPattern (regex), rootHint [x,y] (drawing coords near the inlet), plan view: pipeLayers, headBlocks, headLayers, planHeightM; PDF: pages [1,2].

entry.description: zip only: entry name (or part of it) to show

ids.description: show: only these segment / node / run ids

component.description: show: only this connected component (0 = main network)

tools.name: spr_import_network
tools.description: Create the recognised (or a hand-written) pipe network in the sprinkler module in ONE undo step: nodes, pipes (nominal size, pipe standard, C, line number, valves), nozzles (kind closed|open|drain, K, required pressure, zone, line), drains and the water source. From a drawing: candidateId (+ components, excludeSegments/Nodes/Lines/Runs, source, defaults, drains, nozzleOverrides, zoneByLine/Run/Component, valves, placement). Hand-written: network = {version:1, units:"m", nodes:[{ref,x,y,z}], pipes:[{from,to,diameter,lineNo}], heads:[{node,kind,kFactor,requiredPressure,zone}], sources:[{node,sourceType,…}]}. Water-spray ISO nozzles default to open K80 (project default: general K80, zone deluge — confirm with the user). Validates first (nothing changes on error); dryRun only reports. scriptPath saves the payload JSON (re-import later). mode append (default) | replace. Then spr_run_calc.

network.description: Hand-written import payload (SprImportPayload) instead of candidateId

mode.description: append (default) adds to the current network; replace swaps it (design settings stay)

components.description: Connected components to import (default [0] = main network with the inlet)

excludeSegments.description: Candidate segment ids to drop (drain / air-blow / reference lines …)

source.description: Water source at candidate node (default = recognised inlet): sourceType pump|city_water|gravity_tank|pressure_tank, staticPressure, residualPressure, residualFlow, pumpRatedFlow, pumpRatedHead, pumpShutoffHead (MPa / L/min), tankElevation

defaults.description: kFactor (default 80), nozzleKind (default open for water spray), requiredPressure MPa, material (pipe standard id, e.g. JIS_G3454_STPG_SCH40), cFactor, stemDiameter (25), fallbackDiameter (50)

drains.description: Candidate nodes (open ends) that are drain holes — K or orifice diameter (default = nozzle K: drain hole = sprinkler orifice)

zoneByLine.description: { "<lineNo>": "<zone>" } — nozzles on that line get the zone (zone deluge scenarios)

valves.description: Valves on candidate segments: type, tag (WS-11U), zone (zone valve), open=false (closed)

placement.description: Place the drawing network: x,y,z offset of the inlet (m), rotateDeg about Z, mirrorY, floorIndex (story id; default by z)

scriptPath.description: Also save the import payload JSON to this path ("script" — can be re-imported with network=…)

dryRun.description: Only validate and report counts, change nothing

tools.name: spr_export_results
tools.description: Write the sprinkler / water-spray design results to files: format csv = 5 tables (summary, zones, lines by line number, nozzles, pipes; UTF-8 BOM), fhc = FHC (Canute) calculation-sheet style CSVs (report, heads, pipes, summary, lines, NFPA worksheet, node map), both. scenario = "all" | "zone:<zone>" (default governing scenario), at = supply (actual source) | design (inverse design point). zip=true also writes one zip per format. language = header language (ko default). Uses the current design results or recalculates them. fhcDraft=true adds the FHC project-file draft (.FHC) and pipe data table draft (.PDT) to the FHC files (check them in FHC before use). The FHC files include <name>_bulc_model.csv, which spr_import_fhc_bundle reads back exactly.

outputDir.description: Folder to write into (created if missing)

scenario.description: 'all' or 'zone:<zone>' (default: governing scenario of the design)

zip.description: Also write a zip per format

fhcDraft.description: fhc / both: also write the .FHC project draft + .PDT draft (default false)

slopeMode.description: .FHC draft sloping pipes: horizontal (default — length field = horizontal length), split (horizontal + U/D records), pipe (pipe length)

tools.name: spr_pump_sizing
tools.description: Pump specification for the sprinkler / water-spray network (deterministic). mode from_design (default): from the design calculation (per deluge zone or all-open) → rated flow and pressure with a safety margin, the points the pump curve must pass, NFPA 20 checks (churn ≤ 140 %, ≥ 65 % at 150 % flow), NFPA 20 standard capacity, hydraulic / shaft power and motor kW, NPSHa, pump type, governing zone and nozzle, governing-path losses and re-solved what-if hints (nozzle K −10 %, upsizing the bottleneck, closing drains, valve loss). mode target: a target flow and/or pressure at the source node. mode check_curve: check the network pump curve or a given curve. apply=true writes the proposed curve to the water source (then spr_run_calc).

targetPressureMPa.description: target: pressure at the network source node, MPa

curve.description: check_curve: curve points [{flow L/min, pressure MPa}] (default: the network pump source)

fluid.description: Sea water 1,025 kg/m³ for static heads (marine)

staticLiftM.description: Height of the network source node above the pump centreline, m (+ = pump below)

pumpPipeLossMPa.description: Extra pump → source-node loss at the max design flow, MPa

pumpPipe.description: Pump → source-node pipe {lengthM, diameterMm, material?, cFactor?, equivLengthM?}

suctionHeadM.description: Static suction head m (+ flooded, − lift)

strategy.description: Rated pressure: curve = cover all zone points with the assumed curve (default), envelope = max flow × max pressure

at150RatioPct.description: Assumed curve pressure at 150 % flow, % of rated (default 70)

apply.description: Write the proposed pump curve to the water source (one source)

tools.name: spr_design_review
tools.description: Specification and design-error review of the sprinkler / water-spray network and its design results (deterministic). Checks: pipe pressure rating by standard (KS D 3507 1.2 MPa NFTC 103, SGP, B31.1 wall formula, CuNi/GRE ratings), valve / flange class (JIS 5K/10K/16K/20K, PN, ASME class from valve std/tag), velocities vs limits, nozzles below required / above max pressure, imbalance, drains, closed valves isolating nozzles, disconnected / orphan / dead-end / coincident nodes, zero-length or duplicate pipes, expansion against flow, tee imbalance, high-loss valves, standards / sizes / C / K / required pressure data, zones and zone valves, stories and risers, pump curve NFPA 20 and run-out. Each finding: severity, category, location, message, suggested fix, ids.

category.description: spec = 사양 검토, design = 설계 오류 검토 (default all)

severity.description: List only this severity (e.g. warning — errors no longer fill the list)

code.description: List only this finding code (see byCode)

defaultFlangeClass.description: Class for valves / flanges without a marking

corrosionAllowanceMm.description: Wall corrosion allowance mm (default carbon steel 1.0)

limit.description: Findings to list (default: all when ≤ 100, else 40). byCode always summarises every code

tools.name: spr_import_fhc_bundle
tools.description: Load a BULC "FHC-style" export bundle back (zip, folder of CSVs, or *_bulc_model.csv). mode check (default) changes nothing: compares the bundle network and settings field by field with the CURRENT network, recalculates the bundle network and compares with the results written in the file (nozzle flows / pressures, required source pressure, summary). mode apply replaces the current pipe network with the bundle (undo history cleared, like opening a file) and runs the design calculation. Older bundles without bulc_model can only be partly restored (allowPartial). This is NOT an importer for files saved by the FHC (Canute) program.

allowPartial.description: apply: also load an older bundle without bulc_model (partial network)

recalc.description: apply: run the design calculation after loading (default true)

tools.name: shape_extrude_sketch
tools.description: Shape Studio (SketchUp-style): draw closed 2D loops on ANY plane and extrude them along the plane normal. plane = {origin:[x,y,z], normal:[nx,ny,nz], x_axis:[ax,ay,az]} (x_axis ⟂ normal; y = normal × x_axis); loops = [[[u,v],...], ...] in plane coords, even-odd fill so inner loops become holes. distance (m, sign = along/against normal). mode "new" makes a separate solid; "add"/"cut" fuses into / carves out of target_id (the result replaces target in the tree). Booleans are watertight (manifold kernel), so coplanar faces are fine.

tools.name: shape_push_pull
tools.description: Shape Studio (SketchUp Push/Pull): pick a flat face of node_id and push it in (negative distance → carves) or pull it out (positive → extends the solid). The face is the whole coplanar region reached from the triangle whose outward normal matches face ("+x","-x","+y","-y","+z","-z" or [nx,ny,nz]); point [x,y,z] selects among several faces facing that way (nearest wins), otherwise the outermost one. Works on any node, including results of earlier push/pulls and booleans. Example: box then shape_push_pull(face:"+z", distance:0.5) raises the top by 0.5 m.

tools.name: shape_add_revolve
tools.description: Shape Studio: revolve a half-profile around the z axis — like FreeCAD Revolution. points=[[radius,z],...] radius>=0, top-to-bottom order. angle_deg default 360.

tools.name: shape_add_arch
tools.description: Shape Studio: add an ARCHED / VAULTED / SEMICIRCULAR ceiling (barrel vault, dome-roof tunnel) in ONE call — a curved shell whose inner surface is a circular arc of clear width `span` and inner height `rise` above the springing line (rise = span/2 → semicircle; smaller → shallow segmental arch), extruded `length` metres along `axis`. Use this whenever the user asks for a round/arched/curved/semicircular ceiling or tunnel roof instead of composing primitives. Placement: `start` = coordinate along the axis where the arch begins, `center` = transverse coordinate of the arch centre line, `z_base` = height of the springing line (0 = arch rises from the floor; for a room use the wall-top height). Afterwards export it with shape_export_geom (exact curved &GEOM for the cut-cell solver) or shape_export_obst (voxelised). Units: metres.

span.description: Inner clear width (m), e.g. tunnel width

rise.description: Inner arch height above the springing line (m). Default span/2 (semicircle).

start.description: Axis coordinate where the arch begins (m). Default 0

center.description: Transverse coordinate of the arch centre line (m). Default 0

tools.name: shape_boolean

tools.name: shape_edit_node
tools.description: Shape Studio: rename / show-hide / assign FDS SURF / set color / mark fire faces + fire properties of a node. fire_faces: 6 booleans in FDS SURF_ID6 order [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] OR face-name strings like ["-Z"] ("bottom"/"top" aliases ok); [] clears. Fire faces render as red hatching in the viewport and are wired to a FIRE SURF (+ RAMP_Q / &REAC) on shape_export_obst. Fire properties (merged individually, unspecified keys keep their previous value): fire_hrrpua, fire_tmp_front (°C), fire_ramp_points ([[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...] HRR time curve), fire_fuel_type, fire_soot_yield, fire_co_yield, fire_radiative_fraction, fire_ext_coeff. ONE FIRE OBST PER DOCUMENT: fire faces may exist on only one shape — assigning them to another node automatically clears the previous node's fire faces. PLAN FIRST: real FDS can only apply a fire SURF to a FLAT face (never a curved or stepped one), so setting fire_faces without plan_confirmed changes nothing (the fire_* properties in the same call are dropped too) and returns a 6-direction flatness analysis instead — discuss it with the user, agree on which flat face, HRRPUA, RAMP and combustion properties, then call again with plan_confirmed=true.

fire_faces.description: [-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z] booleans or face names, [] to clear. Only ONE node per document may have fire faces (others are cleared automatically)

fire_hrrpua.description: Fire face HRRPUA kW/m² (default 1000 at export)

fire_ramp_points.description: HRR time curve for RAMP_Q: [[t_seconds, fraction_0..1], ...]

fire_fuel_type.description: Fuel PRESET id — WOOD_OAK, POLYURETHANE_FOAM, COTTON, NYLON, POLYPROPYLENE, PVC, PMMA, GASOLINE. Prefer a preset id: export then writes &REAC FUEL plus the matching C/H/O/N, soot/CO yield and radiative fraction. Any other string is passed through as a raw FUEL name with no chemistry.

plan_confirmed.description: Set true only AFTER the user agreed on the flat fire face and the fire properties (required to actually apply fire_faces and the fire_* properties sent with it)

tools.name: shape_export_obst
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS: voxelize the shape (node_id, or union of all visible roots) and add it to the model as an obstacle with voxel geometry. Recommended: align_to_mesh=true — voxels then use the project MESH cell size and sit exactly on FDS cell boundaries (no ±1 cell snapping). Otherwise voxel_size (m, e.g. 0.1) or per-axis cell [dx,dy,dz]. voxel_mode "shell" voxelizes only the surface (hollow meshes such as hoods, ducts, funnels, open imported STL); default "solid" fills the inside. origin optionally repositions the bbox min corner in the domain (breaks mesh alignment).

voxel_size.description: Voxel edge (m), e.g. 0.1 — ignored when align_to_mesh

align_to_mesh.description: Use the (finest) project MESH cell size and grid origin

node_id.description: Node to export (default: union of visible roots)

origin.description: Domain position of bbox min corner (default: keep authored coords)

surf_id.description: SURF for all faces (default: node surf or INERT)

tools.name: shape_export_geom
tools.description: Shape Studio → FDS cut-cell: export the exact CSG mesh as an &GEOM triangulated surface — no voxelization, so slopes and curves keep their true shape instead of being stair-stepped like shape_export_obst. Only a watertight surface is exported: primitives, hull, array, mirror and non-overlapping unions are fine, but an OVERLAPPING boolean (union/subtract/intersect) always leaves an open seam the CSG library cannot close, so the export is refused — voxelize those with shape_export_obst instead. Needs a GPU engine build with cut-cell support; older engines parse &GEOM but ignore it. Fire (HRRPUA) on a GEOM surface is not supported yet — use shape_export_obst for the burner. Units m, z-up. Default: every visible root, each keeping its own SURF; origin repositions the bbox min corner.

geom_id.description: New &GEOM ID (re-exporting with the same ID replaces it)

node_id.description: Node to export (default: union of visible roots, per-node SURF kept)

surf_id.description: SURF for all faces (default: per-node SURF, else FDS default surface)

origin.description: Domain position of bbox min corner (default: keep authored coords)

rgb.description: Display colour 0-255 (default: let Smokeview use the SURF colour)

allow_open.description: Write the &GEOM even when the surface has holes. Not recommended: FDS stops with ERROR(730) and the GPU cut-cell solver mis-classifies inside/outside

tools.name: shape_export_stl
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD (OpenFOAM etc.): export the exact CSG mesh as STL (no voxelization). ascii=true for text STL with solid name (snappyHexMesh patch name). Units m, z-up.

tools.name: shape_export_obj
tools.description: Shape Studio → CFD: export the exact CSG mesh as OBJ (no voxelization). Units m, z-up.

tools.description: Item library: set FDS fire/material properties on a registered item (shown via the item panel's 'Library FDS Properties' button and applied when the item is placed). Sets a 'fire' preset override.

tools.name: shape_get_item_fds_props
tools.description: Item library: read the FDS properties and metadata of a registered item.

tools.name: shape_screenshot
tools.description: Shape Studio: capture a screenshot of the running GUI (Shape Studio opens automatically) so you can visually REVIEW the shape you built. Returns a PNG file path — read the image, compare against reference photos, then fix with shape_set_params. select_node opens that node in the property panel first (e.g. to review fire faces / HRR chart). Live GUI mode only.

select_node.description: Node id to select before capture (shows its property panel)

tools.name: shape_preview_voxels
tools.description: Shape Studio: switch the viewport into FDS voxel preview mode — it shows exactly what the shape becomes once voxelized into FDS OBST boxes (including the fire faces). size = voxel edge in metres (default 0.1), off=true returns to the smooth CSG view. Call this before shape_screenshot to review the FDS result rather than the ideal mesh. GUI only (no effect headless).

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Read the open project: file path, unsaved changes, CHID, deck path used for runs, stories (id, name, zMin, height, EVAC floorIndex), domain and mesh cells, object counts per module. Call this first in a session and after project_open. Read-only.

tools.name: project_open
tools.description: Open a .bulc project or a .fds deck in the running BULC app (same as File > Open, including evacuation, drawing, sprinkler and HVAC side files). path must be absolute. Refuses when the open project has unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved=true (ask the user first). Live app only.

path.description: Absolute path of a .bulc or .fds file

discard_unsaved.description: Discard unsaved changes of the current project (default false)

tools.name: project_save
tools.description: Save the open project as a .bulc bundle (.bulc + .fds + _evac.json + _spr.json + _hvac.json) like File > Save. Without path it saves to the current .bulc file. A new path must end with .bulc; an existing file is only replaced with overwrite=true. Saving renames CHID to the file name (GEN-009) — result files follow it. Live app only.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at a new path (default false)

tools.name: project_new
tools.description: Start a new empty project in the running app (File > New): clears geometry, evacuation, sprinkler, HVAC and drawing state. Refuses when there are unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved=true. Live app only.

tools.name: project_export_fds
tools.description: Write the current model as an FDS 6.10.1 input deck (.fds) to path (absolute, must end with .fds). CHID becomes the file name. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite=true. To only read the deck use preview_fds. Live app only.

tools.name: project_undo
tools.description: Undo the last model edit(s) of the fire model (obstacles, holes, vents, devices, settings …) like Ctrl+Z. steps 1–20 (default 1). Sprinkler/HVAC/evacuation module edits have their own tools.

tools.name: project_redo
tools.description: Redo model edits undone with project_undo (Ctrl+Y). steps 1–20 (default 1).

tools.name: get_conventions
tools.description: Units, coordinate axes, story / floorIndex numbering, id rules and file conventions used by the BULC tools (they differ between modules — read this before building a model from a drawing). topic = units | coordinates | floors | ids | files | aset | all (default all). Read-only.

tools.name: fds_apply_text
tools.description: Apply an edited FDS deck to the project: send the complete .fds text (start from preview_fds, edit, send back). The deck is parsed and compared section by section with the current model; only changed sections (meshes, obstacles, vents, devices, controls, dump …) are applied, untouched sections keep their app metadata (changed sections are replaced by the parsed values). dryRun (default true) only reports the changed sections. sections limits which top-level sections may change. Nothing changes on a parse error.

tools.name: sim_preflight
tools.description: Pre-run check with structured results: every issue carries a knowledge-pack rule id (e.g. OUT-001, VENT-001, MESH-002). Combines validate_project, the run dialog deck checks (output intervals ≥ T_END, deck reference errors CPU FDS rejects, fires outside the mesh, spray keys the chosen GPU solver ignores, LOCK_TIME_STEP stability hint) and grid resolution advice (D*/dx from the peak HRR). ok=false means do not run. solver = gpu (default) | gpu_cutcell | cpu_openmp. Read-only.

tools.name: sim_start
tools.description: Start the fire simulation in the running app after the user agreed (confirm=true required). Runs sim_preflight first and refuses on errors (force=true only if the user explicitly accepts). The deck is written next to the saved project (.bulc → .fds, like the toolbar RUN) or, for an unsaved project, to Documents/bulc_<folder>/. Refuses while another run is active. solver = gpu (default) | gpu_cutcell | cpu_openmp; restart=true resumes from the checkpoint. Then poll sim_status. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

location.description: project (default when the project is saved) | documents

restart.description: Resume from the restart checkpoint (default false)

force.description: Start even if sim_preflight reports errors (default false)

tools.name: sim_status
tools.description: Status of the current / last fire simulation of this app session: running or finished, exit code, simulated time vs T_END (percent, ETA), step, dt, CFL, HRR (kW), Tmax (K), max velocity, NaN count, health flags (nan=0, Tmax ≤ 2500 K, |u| < 50 m/s) and sprinkler / detector activation times read from the engine log. Read-only.

tools.name: sim_stop
tools.description: Stop the running fire simulation (confirm=true). mode graceful (default) writes <CHID>.stop so the engine finishes its output files and a restart checkpoint; mode kill ends the process at once (results may be incomplete). Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

tools.name: sim_log_tail
tools.description: Last lines of the engine console output of the current / last run (lines ≤ 500, default 60). grep = optional regular expression filter. Read-only.

grep.description: Only lines matching this regular expression (case-insensitive)

tools.name: results_detect
tools.description: Find the result files of a deck (named by its &HEAD CHID, next to the .fds): .smv, _hrr.csv, _devc.csv, _ctrl.csv, .out, and list the slice planes (quantity + plane), Plot3D times / quantities, Smoke3D, boundary and particle files. Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_results_summary
tools.description: Summarise a finished (or running) fire simulation from its result files: peak HRR and time, total heat released (MJ), radiative fraction, last simulated time vs T_END, every device column (max, time of max, final, unit), first time each device with a setpoint reached it, sprinkler / detector activation times from the engine log of this session, and the available output files. Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_timeseries
tools.description: Time series from the result CSV files: file = hrr (HRR, Q_RADI, MLR …) | devc (device ids) | ctrl. columns = column names (default the first 6). t0 / t1 limit the time window; maxPoints ≤ 500 (default 300 — longer series are reduced by time-averaging). Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

tools.name: fire_compute_aset
tools.description: Available safe egress time (ASET) at breathing height: for each point (default: every user exit — OPEN vents, door items, Door_/Window_ holes) the time series at floor + samplingHeight (default 1.8 m) is read from horizontal slices (preferred) or Plot3D and compared with the criteria (default temperature 60 °C, visibility 5 m, CO 1,400 ppm, O2 15 %, CO2 5 %; same as the app ASET report). Returns ASET per point, the governing criterion, a lower bound when no criterion is exceeded, and which quantities are missing (then add output_add_tenability_slices and re-run). points[].floorZ = floor elevation of that point (or story = story id). Read-only.

fdsPath.description: Absolute .fds path (default: the project deck / last run)

source.description: Data source (default auto: slices, then Plot3D)

tools.name: output_add_tenability_slices
tools.description: Add the horizontal slices the ASET check needs at floor + height (default 1.8 m) on every story (or the given story ids / absolute z): TEMPERATURE, VISIBILITY and VOLUME FRACTION of OXYGEN, CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON MONOXIDE (quantities can be limited). Existing identical slices are skipped. Run before sim_start (OUT-006, ASET-004).

z.description: Absolute plane heights instead of stories

height.description: Height above each story floor (default 1.8 m)

tools.name: capture_view
tools.description: Screenshot of the running app for visual checking: view = current (default) | 2d (plan of a story) | 3d | result (result viewer) | shape (Shape Studio). story = story id to show in 2D. region = viewport (default, only the drawing area) | window. Returns the PNG as an image (and its path); savePath (absolute .png) also keeps a copy. Live app only.

maxWidth.description: Downscale to this width in pixels (default 1600)

savePath.description: Also save the PNG here (absolute .png path)

tools.name: evac_run
tools.description: Run the evacuation simulation in the running app after the user agreed (confirm=true): builds the same engine input as the EVAC run dialog (agents, exits = OPEN vents / door items / Door_·Window_ holes, walls, stairs → multi-level mode, waypoints, journeys, FED and alarm settings) and starts the engine in the background. Refuses with no agents, and with no user-defined exits unless allowNoExits=true (the engine would then use temporary exits at the domain edges). Poll evac_status, then read evac_get_results. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

outputFolder.description: Folder for the .evac result file (default: the project folder)

allowNoExits.description: Run even without user-defined exits (default false)

tools.name: evac_status
tools.description: Status of the current / last evacuation run of this app session: running or finished, percent, last engine message, error, result summary. Read-only.

tools.name: evac_stop
tools.description: Stop the running evacuation simulation (confirm=true). No result is kept. Live app only.

confirm.description: Must be true — the user has agreed to this action

tools.name: evac_get_results
tools.description: Summary of the last evacuation result in the project (never the raw trajectories): agents, evacuated / remaining, last exit time (the RSET shown in the app), mean and p50/p90/p95 exit times, evacuation start delay from the alarm chain, FED casualties and their causes, and per-exit counts, first/last times and flow (persons/s/m; each agent is assigned to the exit nearest to its last position). detail = summary (default) | exits | agents (agents lists exit times, limit ≤ 500). Read-only.

tools.name: arch_analyze_drawing
tools.description: Read an architectural floor plan (.dxf, .dwg via the bundled converter, vector .pdf, or an image) and recognise the building: units and scale (DXF $INSUNITS, dimension values, PDF scale text), layer roles, wall centrelines with thickness (double-line or single-line walls), doors (swing arcs / door blocks), windows (window layers / blocks), columns, stair areas, room names and story labels. Returns candidateId, a summary and questions to confirm with the user (DRW-001…003). Images and outlined PDFs return needsVision — then read the picture yourself and call arch_import_floorplan_report. show = walls | openings | columns | rooms | levels | layers lists details (offset, limit, ids). Read-only; the file is read on this PC only.

candidateId.description: Re-use an earlier analysis (with options = analyse again)

options.description: Re-analysis options: scaleMmPerUnit (drawing unit → mm; PDF: scale denominator, 1:100 → 100), wallLayers / doorLayers / windowLayers / columnLayers / excludeLayers (layer names), wallStyle auto|double|single, wallThicknessRange [min,max] m (default [0.05,0.6]), defaultWallThickness m (single-line walls, default 0.2), minWallLength m (default 0.3), page (PDF page, default 1).

tools.name: arch_import_building
tools.description: Create the building on one story in ONE undo step: walls as obstacles (axis-aligned box per wall, diagonal walls stair-stepped like the 2D editor), doors as holes 'Door_<prefix>n' (also evacuation exits) and windows as holes 'Win_<prefix>n' at sill height (not exits), optional columns and slabs. Source: candidateId from arch_analyze_drawing (exclude walls / openings by id) or building = {walls:[{start:[x,y],end:[x,y],thickness?,height?}], doors:[{at:[x,y]|wall:n,position:0..1,width?,height?}], windows:[{at|wall,position,width?,sill?,height?}], columns:[{xb:[x1,x2,y1,y2]}|{center,size}]} in metres; wall:n counts from 1 in the order of building.walls (openings that cannot be placed are listed in warnings). story = story id (default current story; z = its zMin, wall height = its height). dryRun defaults to TRUE — report first, confirm with the user, then call again with dryRun:false. mode append (default) | replace (removes what an earlier import with the same idPrefix created).

building.description: Hand-written building spec (metres) instead of candidateId. Door/window wall:n is 1-based (wall 1 = building.walls[0])

zBase.description: Floor elevation instead of the story zMin (m)

transform.description: Placement: origin = 'bbox_min' (default for drawings: lower-left corner of the building) | 'none' | [x,y] in drawing metres; target [x,y] (default [0,0]); rotateDeg about the target (counter-clockwise); mirrorY. Use the same origin for every story drawing of one building.

defaults.description: wallHeight (default: story height), wallThickness (walls without one, default 0.2), doorWidth 0.9, doorHeight 2.1, windowWidth 1.2, windowSill 0.9, windowHeight 1.2, slabThickness 0.2 (m)

include.description: What to create: doors (true), windows (true), columns (true), floorSlab (false — slab just below the story floor), ceilingSlab (false — slab on top of the walls)

maxObstacles.description: Refuse above this many obstacles (default 3000, max 20000)

tools.name: arch_import_floorplan_report
tools.description: Build walls / doors / windows from YOUR reading of a floor-plan picture (image or outlined PDF page — use when arch_analyze_drawing says needsVision). report = {building_width_m (real width of the outer walls), wall_height_m?, wall_thickness_m?, walls:[{x1,y1,x2,y2}] wall CENTRELINES in normalised image coordinates 0..1 (origin top-left, y down; split at corners, skip dimension lines, text, furniture, hatching), doors:[{x,y,width_m?}], windows:[{x,y,width_m?,sill_m?,height_m?}]}. image = {width,height} pixels (or imagePath) for the aspect ratio. The app converts the report with fixed rules (snap to horizontal/vertical, y flipped, origin at the lower-left wall corner) and creates the same objects as arch_import_building. Needs no AI key in the app. dryRun defaults to TRUE.

imagePath.description: Absolute path of the image (its header gives the size)

transform.description: Placement: origin = 'bbox_min' (default for drawings: lower-left corner of the building) | 'none' | [x,y] in drawing metres; target [x,y] (default [0,0]); rotateDeg about the target (counter-clockwise); mirrorY. Use the same origin for every story drawing of one building.

defaults.description: wallHeight (default: story height), wallThickness (walls without one, default 0.2), doorWidth 0.9, doorHeight 2.1, windowWidth 1.2, windowSill 0.9, windowHeight 1.2, slabThickness 0.2 (m)

include.description: What to create: doors (true), windows (true), columns (true), floorSlab (false — slab just below the story floor), ceilingSlab (false — slab on top of the walls)
